text:
alex (release lead): heads-up — deploy-bot flagged a canary regression for model-service v2.7.0 in us-west-2. p95 up ~40%.
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary rollout: model-service v2.7.0 exceeded p95-latency threshold (threshold=200ms, observed=280ms). Suggested action: evaluate rollback.
sam (sre): seeing the same in grafana. CPU on gpu-3 nodes pegging during long context requests. Traces show KV cache churn.
natalie (eng): i pulled a trace — KV miss rate jumped after the new kvcache eviction change. suspect the change in batch alignment in 2.7.0.
mike (pm): how many customers could be affected? any dedicated pools pinned to 2.7.0?
ops-oncall: one dedicated customer in EU was scheduled to upgrade today but still on 2.6.x. Hosted traffic slice (~7%) on canary is impacted.
alex (release lead): decision call: do we auto-rollback or manual pin? We have a change window in ~20m.
sam (sre): i'm not comfortable with autopilot here — we'd lose the telemetry needed to root cause. prefer manual rollback to 2.6.9 and keep canary off until fix.
natalie (eng): agree. we'll need a short patch to revert the eviction heuristic. i'll open PR but manual pin first.
deply-bot (typo intentional in a follow-up?): :confused: (ignore)
deploy-bot: NOTE: If manual rollback selected, run /deploy rollback --service=model-service --to=2.6.9 --scope=canary OR /pin-version --service=model-service --version=2.6.9 --reason="latency spike" for targeted pin.
alex (release lead): ok manual pin. sam — can you execute the pin and coordinate post-rollback smoke? add a rollback note in release notes. mike — you handle customer comms for hosted majority. natalie — prepare the revert PR and add a regression test.
sam (sre): running: ```
/bin/deployctl pin-version --service model-service --version 2.6.9 --scope canary --note "p95 spike: kvcache eviction"
# expecting 1-2 minute rollout to canary
```
sam (sre): pin completed. canary traffic switched back to 2.6.9. verifying metrics now.
sam (sre): p95 back to baseline in ~45s. cpu normalized. :tada:
mike (pm): drafting customer note: "We detected a latency regression affecting a small canary slice during deployment of v2.7.0. We rolled back the canary to v2.6.9 while we investigate. No action required from customers." want to send after we confirm stability.
natalie (eng): PR created: revert-kvcache-heuristic. link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/824 (WIP). adding unit + integration tests.
ops-oncall: updating the change window calendar to reflect manual rollback and follow-up patch deployment tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
alex (release lead): good. mike, please craft the short release note update and post to #customer-briefing once we confirm 30m stability. also add an entry to the rollout runbook: why manual pinned vs auto-rollback.
mike (pm): will do. ping me when 30m stable.
sam (sre): 30m passed — metrics stable, no new error trends. planning to unpin later after natalie's patch validated in staging. :thumbsup:
alex (release lead): closing thread — manual pin executed, customers will be notified, patch queued. thanks team.
